Rashi on Shabbat 81a:1:1.english: A spoon - A spoon, [in Old French:] culier.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:1:2.hebrew: חף - קס"ד דפותחת של חף עצמה, ושיעורה נפיש מתרווד:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:1:2.english: A ḥaf - [The Gemara] initially thought that [it refers to] the key of a latch itself, and its measure is larger than [that of] a spoon.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:1:3.hebrew: כרכר - עץ יש לאורגין, וראשו חד:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:1:3.english: A bobbin - Weavers have a piece of wood, and its tip is sharp.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:1:4.hebrew: כדי לזרוק בבהמה - דלא טרח איניש למשקל צרור משום עוף להבריחו, דבקלא בעלמא דרמי ליה — אזיל ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:1:4.english: [Equivalent] to that which is used to throw at an animal - For a person does not take the trouble to take a pebble on account of a bird to chase it away, since with a mere sound that he directs at it, it goes away.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:1.hebrew: והא קיי"ל דשיעורא דרבנן נפיש - גבי לעשות תלאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:1.english: Don’t we maintain that the measure of the Rabbis is greater? - In the case of "to make a loop [for hanging]" [in the earlier Mishnah (78a)].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:2.hebrew: חפי פותחת - שינים הקבועים בה, ולא היא עצמה; ועושים אותם מעצם:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:2.english: Teeth of a key - The teeth that are fixed in it, and not [the key] itself; and they make them from bone.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:3.hebrew: חפי פותחת טהורין - דכל זמן שלא חברן בה, אינן ראויין לכלום:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:3.english: The teeth of a key are ritually pure - For as long as one has not attached them to it, they are not fit for anything.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:4.hebrew: טמאין - דכלי עצם ככלי מתכות, ופשוטיהן טמאין, בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף כה:). ואי משום דמחובר לפותחת, וכל המחובר לטהור טהור — פותחת יש לה בית קיבול, ומקבל מפתח:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:4.english: [They are] impure - For bone utensils are like metal utensils, and their flat [forms] are impure, [as taught in the chapter] “Hakol Shochetin” (Chullin 25b). And if [one should argue that they should be pure] because [each tooth] is attached to the potachat, and whatever is attached to a pure [utensil] is pure — a potachat has a receptacle, and receives a key.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:5.hebrew: ושל גל - ואם הפותחת הזאת אינה של כלים, כגון של שידה ומגדל, אלא של גל — כמו "טרוקי גלי", כגון דלתות שערי החצר — אע"פ שחברן בפותחת, הואיל וחבור זה בדלת היא, ודלת בנין מחובר לקרקע, טהורין:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:2:5.english: And [those] of a gate - And if this lock is not of vessels, such as of a chest or a wardrobe, but of a gate — like “toroku galei” [shut the gates], such as the doors of courtyard gateways — [then] even though he attached them to the lock, since this attachment is to the door, and the door of a building is attached to the ground, they are [ritually] pure.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:3:1.hebrew: סכוכית - זכוכית. ועל שם שסוכין קרי סכוכית, ועל שם שהיא זכה קרי זכוכית:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:3:1.english: Sekhukhit - [This means] glass [zekhukhit]. And on account of [the fact] that they gaze [sokhin, through it], it is called sekhukhit; and on account of [the fact] that it is clear [zakhah], it is called zekhukhit.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:4:1.english: And that is provided that it feels [it] - The animal [feels] this pebble upon its impact.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:5:1.hebrew: שיעורן בכמה - להתחייב עליהן, אי נמי, לטלטלן בחצר ולהכניסן לבית הכסא. ואידי ואידי חד שיעורא הוא, דבמידי דחזי להו מיחייב על הוצאתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:5:1.english: How much is their measure - [Is it] to become liable for [carrying] them [out], or alternatively, to move them in a courtyard and bring them into the bathroom? And both this and that are the same measure, for one is liable for carrying it out [only] with something that is fit for [use].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:5:2.hebrew: כזית כאגוז כביצה - שלש מכניסין לקינוח, ומקנח זו אחר זו — אחת כזית, ואחת כאגוז, ואחת כביצה. בתחלה מקנח פי הרעי בקטנה, להסיר רעי הנדבק שם, שהגדולה פוחסת ומלכלך סביבותיו:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:5:2.english: An olive-bulk, a nut-bulk, [and] an egg-bulk - Three [stones] are brought in for wiping, and one wipes [with them] one after the other: one [the size of] an olive-bulk, one [the size of] a nut-bulk, and one [the size of] an egg-bulk. Initially, one wipes the opening of the anus with the small [stone] to remove feces adhering there, for the large [stone] squashes [the feces] and soils its surroundings.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:5:3.english: Turtani - Scales. [Will he] bring [them] in there to weigh?

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:5:4.hebrew: מלא היד - בין שלשתן, או אפילו הן ד' וה' — ובין כולן מלא היד:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:5:4.english: A handful - Whether [divided] between the three of them, or even if they are four or five [stones] — and between all of them [combined they total] a handful.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:1.english: Sharpened [stones] - Sharp-edged [Old French: becudes], so that they are suitable for wiping.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:2.hebrew: מותר להכניסם - בתוך ד' אמות או בחצר, דלא ליתסר לטלטולינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:2.english: It is permitted to bring them in - Within four cubits or in a courtyard, so that handling them should not be forbidden.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:3.english: A nut-bulk - Each and every one [of them].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:4.hebrew: התם מתני' - פלוגתא דאתרוג מתני' היא במסכת סוכה, והיא סדורה בפי התלמידים:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:4.english: There, [it is] a Mishnah - The dispute concerning the citron is a Mishnah in Tractate Sukkah, and it is fluent in the mouths of the students.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:5.hebrew: והכא ברייתא - ויש הרבה תלמידים שלא שנאוה, והוא תולה הידועה בשאינה ידועה:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:5.english: And here [it is] a baraita - And there are many students who have not learned it, and [yet] he makes the known dependent upon that which is not known.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:6.hebrew: כך מחלוקת כאן - ולסימנא בעלמא אמרה, דלא תשכח לגירסא דברייתא; ואם תשכחנה, הזכר ממשנתך דאתרוג:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:6:6.english: So too, [there] is a dispute here - And he stated it merely as a mnemonic, so that you will not forget the version of the baraita; and if you forget it, remind yourself from your Mishnah concerning [the] etrog.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:1.hebrew: אבל לא הפאייס - כמו שקל פיסת רגב (סנהדרין דף סד.), שקורין גלישט"א. דהואיל ומיפרכה — לא חזי לקינוח, ואסורה לטלטל:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:1.english: However, not the payis - Like: “He took a clod [pisat] of earth” (Sanhedrin 64a), which they call gleste [a clod of earth]. For since it crumbles, it is not fit for wiping, and it is forbidden to move [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:2.hebrew: כרשיני בבלייתא - הכי מיקרו, משום שבבל ארץ לחה היא, והמחרישה מעלה רגבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:2.english: Babylonian vetches - They are called this because Babylonia is a moist land, and the plow turns up clods [of earth].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:3.hebrew: למשמש - הנצרך ליפנות ואינו יכול ליפנות, אמרינן לקמן בפירקין דממשמש בצרור בנקב והוא נפתח. וקא סלקא דעתך דקאמר: ובשבת אסור למשמש כלל כדרך שממשמשים בחול:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:3.english: To manipulate - [Regarding] one who needs to relieve himself and cannot relieve himself, we say later in our chapter that he manipulates with a pebble at the orifice and it opens. And it initially occurred to [the Gemara] that he was saying: On Shabbat it is forbidden to manipulate at all in the manner that one manipulates on weekdays.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:4.hebrew: ליסתכן - דאמר מר (תמיד פ"א דף כז:): עמוד החוזר מביא אדם לידי הדרוקן:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:4.english: Should he endanger himself? - For the Master said (Tamid, chapter 1, 27b): A column [of feces] that turns back brings a person to dropsy [hidrokan].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:5.hebrew: ומשני כלאחר יד - האי כדרך דקאמר רבא — כדרך הממשמש בחול, בלא שינוי, משום השרת נימין. אבל כלאחר יד, כגון אוחז צרור בב' אצבעותיו — שפיר דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:5.english: And [the Gemara] answers: In an unusual manner - This [phrase], “in the manner,” that Rava said [means] in the manner of one who manipulates on a weekday, without variation, because of detaching hairs. But in an unusual manner, such as holding a pebble with two of his fingers, it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:6.hebrew: אם יש מקום קבוע לבה"כ - שאם ישתיירו לו ערבית, יקנח בהם שחרית — מכניס שם מלא יד:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:6.english: If there is a fixed place for a bathroom - For if [any stones] are left over for him in the evening, he will wipe with them in the morning — [therefore] he may bring in a handful there.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:7.hebrew: כהכרע - כשיעור המכריע, כאגוז — נפיש מכזית וזוטר מכביצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:7.english: Like the intermediate [measure] - Like the intermediate measure: like a nut, [which is] larger than an olive-bulk and smaller than an egg-bulk.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:8.hebrew: מדוכה קטנה - מלאכתה לאיסור, אסור לטלטל:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:8.english: A small mortar - [Since] its function is for a prohibited [purpose], it is forbidden to move [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:9.hebrew: ואם יש עליה עד - קנוח המעיד שעשויה לכך, מותר לטלטלה לקינוח:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:7:9.english: And if it has a witness upon it - [A mark of] wiping that testifies that it is designated for this [purpose], it is permitted to move it for wiping.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:1.english: Hemorrhoids - *Figes* [Old French for figs, referring to hemorrhoids].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:2.hebrew: לולבי גפנים - אותן פיצולין הגדלין בגפן, וקורין וודיל"ש:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:2.english: Tendrils of grapevines - Those offshoots that grow on the vine, and are called vedilles [tendrils].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:3.hebrew: מוריגי בהמה - כל בשר שיש בבהמה העשוי כמורג, שהוא פגום וחרוקה כמורג חרוץ חדש; כלומר: כל מקום שאין הבשר חלק — כגון קליפת הלשון, וכגון החיך שיש בו כמין קוצין וכפגימות, וכבית הכוסות:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:3.english: The threshing sledges of an animal - Any meat on an animal that is shaped like a threshing sledge, in that it is notched and grooved like “a new sharp threshing sledge” [Isaiah 41:15]; that is to say, anywhere that the meat is not smooth — such as the skin of the tongue, and such as the palate, which has thorn-like [protrusions] and indentations, and like the reticulum.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:4.english: With which another cleaned himself - This also applies to lime and to clay:

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:5.hebrew: התולה - שאינו יושב. אלמא, קינח בו חברו לא חזי לקינוח, ורב ששת אמר לעיל: אם יש עליה עד, מותר:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:5.english: One who suspends [himself] - That he does not sit down. Evidently, [a stone with which] one's fellow wiped is not fit for wiping, and [yet] Rav Sheshet said above: If it has a mark upon it, it is permitted.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:6.english: Moist - [A stone that is moist] is not fit [for wiping; when it is] dry, it is fit.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:7.hebrew: מצד אחד - באותו צד שקינח בו חבירו, לא חזי לקינוח; אבל בצד שני, חזי:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:7.english: On one side - On that side with which his fellow wiped, it is not fit for wiping; but on the other side, it is fit.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:8:8.english: His own - That the wiping that was upon it was his own.

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:9:1.english: And were obscured - That indication [of prior use].

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:9:2.hebrew: מהו - מי בטיל לייחוד דידהו, או לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:9:2.english: What is [the ruling]? - Has their designation been nullified, or not?

Rashi on Shabbat 81a:9:3.hebrew: אי רשומו ניכר מותר - דכיון דמאיס, לא חזי לבשמים, ולא מיבטל ליה מבית הכסא:
Rashi on Shabbat 81a:9:3.english: If its mark is discernible, it is permitted - For since it is repulsive, it is not fit for [crushing] spices, and its [designation] for the privy is not nullified.

Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:2:1.hebrew: למימרא דשיעורא דר' יהודה נפיש - ואע"ג דאשכחן תרווד שהוא גדול הרבה, כדאמר בנזיר בפרק כ"ג (דף נ:) גבי מלא תרווד רקב כמה שיעורו: חזקיה אמר מלא פיסת יד, ור' יוחנן אמר מלא חפניו — התם ודאי מיירי בתרווד גדול, כדתנן במסכת כלים בפ' י"ז (משנה. ב): שאמר מידה גסה, מלא תרווד רקב כמלא תרווד גדול של רופאים. אבל הכא, להוצאת שבת, מידי דחשיב בעינן, ותרווד קטן חשוב הוא הרבה. (א"נ): חף סלקא דעתך שהוא חף גל, שהוא גדול; ומשני: בחפי פותחת, שהן קטנים:
Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:2:1.english: Is that to say that the measure of Rabbi Yehuda is greater? - And even though we find that a spoon is very large, as [the Gemara] says in Nazir in chapter [Kohen Gadol] (50b) regarding "a full spoon of corpse-dust, how much is its measure? Chizkiya said: a full palm, and Rabbi Yochanan said: both hands full" — there, it certainly deals with a large spoon, as we learned in tractate Kelim in chapter 17 (Mishnah 2), which stated a gross measure: "a full spoon of corpse-dust is like a full large spoon of physicians." But here, regarding carrying out on Shabbat, we require something that is significant, and [even] a small spoon is very significant. Alternatively, [the Gemara] thought that chaf is the tooth of a lock, which is large, and [Ulla] resolves [the question by explaining that Rabbi Yehuda refers to] the teeth of a key, which are small.

Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:2:2.hebrew: חפי פותחת טהורין - פי' בקונטרס: שינים של עצם, ונותנין אותם בפותחת לפתוח, וקודם שלא נקבעו אין ראוין לכלום; קבען בפותחת — טמאין, דכלי עצם כמתכות ופשוטיהם טמאים, כדאמר בהכל שוחטין (חול. ן דף כה:); ואי משום דמחובר לפותחת, והמחובר לטהור טהור — פותחת יש לה בית קיבול, דמקבלת מפתח. ומה שפירש דפשוטי כלי עצם טמאים כדאמר בהכל שוחטין — לא דק, דהתם לא איירי אלא בגולמי כלי עצם; אבל פשוטי כלי עצם, הא תנן, ומייתי לה בפ"ק (דף טז:): כלי עץ, כלי עור, כלי עצם, כלי זכוכית — פשוטיהן טהורין. ומה שפירש דחפין הן של עצם — קשה לר"י, דגבי כלי מתכות מיתניא בתוספתא דכלים. ועוד, דאי בשלא נקבעו אין ראויין לכלום — אם כן פשיטא דטהורין! ומה שפי' שפותחת יש לה בית קיבול לקבל המפתח — הא לא חשיב בית קיבול, שאין המפתח עשוי לטלטל ע"י אותו בית קיבול; כמו הקיטע יוצא בקב שלו (לעיל שבת דף סו.) דטהור כשאין בו בית קיבול כתיתין, דפי' בקונט' דמה שמניח ראש שוקו בתוכו לא חשיב בית קיבול, שאין השוק מיטלטל על ידו. ועוד, דפי' דפותחת גורמת טומאה לחף — אדרבה, תנן במס' כלים בפי"ג (משנה ו): פותחת של עץ וחפין של מתכת טמאה, פותחת של מתכת וחפין שלה של עץ טהורה, אלמא בתר חפין אזלינן! ואע"ג דמשמע דאתיא כרבי נחמיה, דלא אזיל בתר מעמיד אלא בתר תשמיש, דהיינו חותם — ברייתא דשמעתי' נמי נראה לר"י דאתיא כוותיה, דקתני סיפא דהכא: טבעת של מתכת וחותם של אילמג, ר' נחמיה מטהר. ונראה לר"י דבחפין של מתכת איירי, ואע"פ שלא נקבעו ראויין הם קצת ליתנם בפותחת, ואפילו הכי טהורין, דגולמי כלי מתכות טהורין; קבען בפותחת — טמאין, שנגמרה מלאכתן. וכן משמע בסמוך דטעמא משום גמר מלאכה, דקתני: ושל גל אע"פ שחברן לדלת כו', דמשמע מה שקבען לדלת יש לו לגרום טומאה, אלא כיון שאין להם פותחת [וחף] קבוע בגל — טהור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:2:2.english:
The teeth of a key are ritually pure - The Kuntres explained: Teeth of bone, and they place them into the key to open [the lock], and before they are affixed they are not fit for anything. [If] one affixed them to the key, they are impure, for bone utensils are like metal [utensils] and their flat forms are susceptible to ritual impurity, as [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] Hakol Shochtin (Chullin 25b). And if [you object that it should be pure] because it is attached to the key, and whatever is attached to something ritually pure is pure — the key has a receptacle, as it receives the key.
And that which he explained that flat bone utensils are impure, as it says in Hakol Shochtin — he was not precise, for there it is dealing only with unfinished bone utensils; but flat bone utensils, behold we learned [in a Mishnah], and [the Gemara] cites it in the first chapter (16b): Utensils of wood, utensils of leather, utensils of bone, [and] utensils of glass — their flat forms are pure.
And that which he explained that the teeth are of bone — [this is] difficult to the Ri, for it is taught among [the laws of] metal utensils in the Tosefta of Kelim.
And furthermore, if when they are not affixed they are not fit for anything — if so, it is obvious that they are pure!
And that which he explained that the key has a receptacle to receive the key — this is not considered a receptacle, for the key is not made to be moved by means of that receptacle; just like "an amputee may go out with his wooden leg" (above, Shabbat 66a), which is pure when it does not have a receptacle for pads, where the Kuntres explained that [the fact] that he places the top of his stump into it is not considered a receptacle, since the leg is not moved by means of it.
And furthermore, that he explained that the key causes ritual impurity to the teeth — on the contrary, we learned in tractate Kelim in chapter 13 (Mishnah 6): A wooden key whose teeth are of metal is impure; a metal key whose teeth are of wood is pure. Thus we see that we follow the teeth!
And even though it implies that this follows Rabbi Nechemiah, who does not follow the supporting frame but rather follows the [primary] function, which is the seal — the baraita of our sugya also appears to the Ri to follow his view, for the latter clause teaches here: A ring of metal and a seal of coral — Rabbi Nechemiah purifies [it].
And it appears to the Ri that it is dealing with teeth of metal, and even though they were not affixed, they are somewhat fit to be placed into the key, and even so they are pure, because unfinished metal utensils are pure. [When] one affixed them to the key, they are impure, because their manufacture is completed.
And so it is implied nearby that the reason is due to the completion of manufacture, as it teaches: "And [teeth] of a lock, even though one attached them to the door, etc.," which implies that [the fact] that he affixed them to the door ought to cause ritual impurity; rather, since they do not have a key, [and the tooth] is affixed to the lock, it is pure.

Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:7:1.hebrew: אסור למשמש בצרור - פירש בקונטרס: הנצרך לפנות ואינו יכול, אסור משום השרת נימין. וא"ת: והא רבא בדבר שאין מתכוין סבר כר"ש בספ"ב דביצה (דף כג.), וכה"ג פריך לקמן לרבי יוחנן דאסר משום השרת נימין? ויש לומר: דהכא במשמוש צרור הוי פסיק רישיה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:7:1.english: It is prohibited to manipulate with a stone - Rashi explained: [This refers to] one who needs to relieve himself and cannot; [and] it is prohibited due to the shedding of hairs. And if you say: But doesn't Rava hold in accordance with Rabbi Shimon regarding an unintentional act [that it is permitted], at the end of the second chapter of Beitzah (23b), and [the Gemara] poses a similar objection later on to Rabbi Yochanan, who prohibited [it] due to the shedding of hairs? And one can say: Here, with the manipulation of a stone, it is a pesik reishei [an inevitable outcome].

Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:7:2.hebrew: ואם לאו כהכרע - ונראה לר"ת כגירסת ר"ח: "ואם לאו כהכרע מדוכה קטנה של בשמים". והכרע — פי' רגל, כמו כרעי המטה. וכן מפרש בירושלמי: "כמלא רגל מדוכה קטנה של בשמים":
Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:7:2.english: "And if not, like an hekhre'a" - And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam like the reading of Rabbeinu Chananel: "And if not, like the hekhre'a of a small mortar for spices." And hekhre'a means a leg, like "the legs of the bed." And so it is explained in the Yerushalmi: "Like the full [size of the] leg of a small mortar for spices."

Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:7:3.hebrew: אמר רב ששת אם יש עליה עד מותר - מילתא באפי נפשה היא. פירוש: מותר לקנח בה אפילו גדולה יותר מכביצה, או אם יש הרבה ממלא היד — מותר ליטול כולן, דכיון דיש עליהן עד, הוכנו כולן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 81a:7:3.english: Rav Sheshet said: If it has an indication on it, it is permitted - This is an independent statement. Explanation: It is permitted to wipe with it even if [it is] larger than an egg; or, if there are more than a handful, it is permitted to take all of them, for since there is an indication on them, they have all been designated.
